0.content:
Broken Isle: Broken Isle is a limited-time island cluster in the west of the Golden Apple Archipelago, the summer-event map east of Mondstadt. Its main island has five peaks with differing water levels, linked to a group of rocks that ring a melody at high tide. It appeared in the Midsummer Island Adventure event (1.6) and again, redesigned, in Summertime Odyssey (2.8).

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1. Both event runs ended (1.6 in June 2021, 2.8 in August 2022).

1.content:
Broken Sea: The Broken Sea is an area of Simulanka, the storybook world of the limited-time Summertide Scales and Tales event (4.8). It is unlocked during the quest Until the End of the World (Page III). People are stranded around it, and a boat there is one way to leave the book's world.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; the event ended on 2024-08-28.

2.content:
Constellation Metropole: Constellation Metropole is a royal city of toy figures in Simulanka, the storybook world of the limited-time Summertide Scales and Tales event (4.8). In the story Navia is its king, and the stars are missing from its sky. It has a Maritime Express station, a gear-driven lift and a statue of the Goddess of Prophecy.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; the event ended on 2024-08-28.

3.content: Cool Isle (also: Cool Isle realm layout): Cool Isle is one of the three Realm Layouts offered when the Serenitea Pot is first unlocked: a cluster of islands surrounded by water inside the teapot. The game's own blurb wonders how many cups of tea such a vast ocean could brew. It came with the Serenitea Pot in Version 1.5.

4.content: Dark Sea (also: Dark Outer Sea, other-shore): The Dark Sea is Teyvat's name for everything beyond the continent and the Seven's dominion: unknown lands and seas, not only water. After the Archon War ended about 2,000 years ago, many defeated gods who refused to live under the Seven fled there and came to be called evil gods.

5.content:
Domain (also: Domains, Secret Realm, Trounce Domain, Quest Domain, One-Time Domain, Domain of Blessing, Domain of Forgery, Domain of Mastery): Domains are self-contained pocket areas that adventurers enter through temple-like gateways, caves or broken structures scattered across Teyvat. Inside are combat trials, puzzles or powerful guardians, and at the end a reward. They are found in every region. Canon never explains in-world what they are, so treat them as mysterious, bounded places rather than a known institution.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 domains remain a standard part of adventuring in every region.

6.content: Emerald Peak (also: Emerald Peak realm layout): Emerald Peak is a mountain Realm Layout in the Serenitea Pot, one of the three offered by default. The game describes a cloud-piercing summit, then jokes that inside a teapot the tallest mountain probably reaches no higher than the stalk of a tea leaf. It was added in Version 1.5 with the Serenitea Pot.

7.content: Floating Abode (also: Floating Abode realm layout): Floating Abode is one of the three default Realm Layouts of the Serenitea Pot: a cluster of islands suspended in mid-air. The game calls this a typical feature of many adepti realms, a boundless world with nothing but a cluster of islands. It arrived in Version 1.5 with the Serenitea Pot.

8.content:
Forest of Blessings (also: Kingdom of Breezes and Bells): The Forest of Blessings is the first area of Simulanka, the storybook world of the limited-time Summertide Scales and Tales event (4.8). Its wildlife is made of folded paper: frogs, hamsters, alpacas and flying squirrels. It holds the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells, a Hut of Blessings and a railway platform from which the Maritime Express runs to Constellation Metropole.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; the event ended on 2024-08-28.

9.content: Memory Core (also: Temple of Space: Memory Core): The Memory Core is a huge storage device at the centre of the Temple of Space, in the Pillar Hall Central Zone. It holds information about civilizations that have passed out of human memory. Travelers offer it Memory Factors, the ember-like remains of forgotten creations, and receive rewards in return.

10.content:
Minacious Isle: Minacious Isle is a limited-time island in the southwest of the Golden Apple Archipelago. According to Albedo, its main island used to be a mountain of Mondstadt that was ripped away and landed in the sea upside down. It has inverted ruins, dandelions, Anemo enemies and a way back to Mondstadt, and appeared in the 1.6 and 2.8 summer events.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; it existed only during the 1.6 and 2.8 event runs.

11.content:
Nod-Krai (also: Nephilheim, Nod Krai, Nod-Kraian): Nod-Krai is an autonomous region on the southernmost edge of Snezhnaya, in Teyvat's northwest: cold islands, desolate tundra, snowy groves and long, dark nights. It has no Archon and no true government. People from all over Teyvat gather in its scrap-metal port, Nasha Town, which gives the land a reputation as a lawless "Elysium". The Frostmoon Scions, its indigenous people, worship the Moon Goddess Kuutar, the former Fatui Harbinger Columbina. The land is soaked in kuuvahki, the power of the moons, and since the Cataclysm it has been plagued by the Abyssal Wild Hunt.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Nod-Krai is at peace again and rebuilding. Dottore was destroyed in the Song of the Welkin Moon crisis. The real Frost Moon has been pulled back inside Teyvat's sky, and Columbina lives openly among the Frostmoon Scions on Hiisi Island. The Wild Hunt has lost its leaders but still roams. The Traveler has moved on to Snezhnaya.

12.content:
Pudding Isle: Pudding Isle is a limited-time island in the east of the Golden Apple Archipelago, the summer-event map east of Mondstadt. It was the island where the player started in Midsummer Island Adventure (1.6) and, in Summertime Odyssey (2.8), an island whose halves a bonsai could switch between Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma styles.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; limited to the 1.6 and 2.8 event runs.

13.content: Shadowflit Archipelago (also: Shadowflit Archipelago realm layout): Shadowflit Archipelago is the Nod-Krai-themed Realm Layout of the Serenitea Pot, added in Version Luna V (6.4, released 2026-02-25). The game describes a complicated group of islands hovering high in the sky, drawn together by some mysterious mechanism.

14.content: Silken Courtyard (also: Silken Courtyard realm layout): Silken Courtyard is an Inazuma-themed Realm Layout added to the Serenitea Pot in Version 2.2. The game says its charm comes from overlapping patchworks of mountains and waters and the elegant scent of tea in the air. It is unlocked with the Silken Print, a prayer plaque of Inazuman scenery carved on Yumemiru wood.

15.content: Simulanka: Simulanka is a storybook world created by the Hexenzirkel witches Alice, Barbeloth and Andersdotter, whom its people call the Goddesses of Creation, Prophecy and Fate. In the limited 4.8 event Summertide Scales and Tales, a strange book sent by Alice pulled the Traveler, Paimon and several friends into it to save the world from an evil dragon. Visions do not work there.

16.content: Skirk's Planet (also: Skirk's homeland, Skirk's home planet): Skirk's planet is the world in the sea of stars where the swordswoman Skirk was born. It began as a hostile world whose extreme temperatures could not support life, yet humans emerged there and evolved the ability to adapt to any environment or energy source. A merchant ship from a neighbouring planet was welcomed, discovered that ability and judged the people a threat, and an army then destroyed them. The planet is unnamed and cannot be visited; it is known only from Skirk's memories in her Crystallina Chapter (5.7).

17.content: Sublime Spicewood (also: Sublime Spicewood realm layout): Sublime Spicewood is the Sumeru-themed Realm Layout, added in Version 3.2. The game pictures the branches and leaves of a towering tree hanging high above a sea of clouds, immense and sturdy, with a wondrous floral fragrance lingering evermore.

18.content: Swirling Isles (also: Swirling Isles realm layout): Swirling Isles is the Fontaine-themed Realm Layout, added in Version 4.3: a wondrous deepwater archipelago, silent and serene, with a multitude of lights swirling about. Inside the realm it is always night, whatever hour the clock shows.

19.content:
Temple of Space (also: Segment-Domain Tau, Hall of Emptiness): The Temple of Space, which its maker named "Segment-Domain Tau", is a vast temple floating unseen in the sky above Windrest Peak in northern Mondstadt. It belongs to Asmoday, the Ruler of Space. She turned it into an exhibition hall for vanished civilisations. People, relics, landscapes and even whole ecosystems from past ages were "uplifted" into it and kept there, unchanging, as living memories. Inside, time stands still: nobody ages, hungers, tires or dies. Asmoday has been gone for a long time. The Watcher Melanta then ruled the temple harshly until the Traveler defeated him in 6.5.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple is free of Melanta's rule and still floats hidden above Windrest Peak, with its uplifted residents still living there. Asmoday has not returned.

20.content:
Teyvat: Teyvat is the world of the story, a planet and the continent on it, where the seven elements (Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro, Hydro, Pyro, Cryo) flow. It has seven nations, each tied to one element, one ideal and one god of The Seven (the Archons): Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan and Snezhnaya. Above it floats Celestia, seat of the Heavenly Principles, who have ruled the world since conquering it in the distant past. Ordinary people may receive a Vision that lets them wield an element. 500 years ago the fall of the godless underground kingdom Khaenri'ah, the cataclysm, unleashed the Abyss on every nation. That calamity has ended, but peace has not fully returned.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Archon Quest is in Snezhnaya (Chapter VII). The Heavenly Principles still sleep. The Tsaritsa's Fatui hold six of the seven Gnoses and are openly preparing to challenge Celestia. The Frost Moon has returned to Teyvat's sky.

21.content: The Sea of Flowers at the End (also: Sea of Flowers at the End, Sea of Flowers of the End): The Sea of Flowers at the End is a place where Inteyvat flowers, the national flower of Khaenri'ah, bloom in full. The Traveler's sibling found it at the end of their long journey. The Traveler had once said they wished to find such a place in the universe, so its discovery moved the sibling to stop travelling with the Traveler and take up Teyvat's affairs.

22.content: Tletl Ilhuicatl (also: Tletl Ilhuicatl realm layout): Tletl Ilhuicatl is the Natlan-themed Realm Layout, added in Version 5.3. The game places it high above a sea of clouds, where towering peaks bask in scorching sunlight and the air is full of endless heat. The name is Nahuatl, from words for 'fire' and 'sky'.

23.content:
Tower of Radiant Light (also: Brilliant Light Tower): The Tower of Radiant Light is a large tower in Luyang Academy, the painting gallery of the Temple of Space. The Traveler climbs it during the quest Long Live Life, in the effort to restore the Academy.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Academy is restored and its painters are free; the tower has no further role in the story.

24.content:
Twinning Isle: Twinning Isle is a limited-time island group in the northeast of the Golden Apple Archipelago, the summer-event map east of Mondstadt. In the 1.6 Midsummer Island Adventure it was a cluster of fog-wrapped islets and a central stage with a samurai puppet; in 2.8 Summertime Odyssey it held a castle of Night Ravens connected with Fischl's imagination.

Status as of 7.1: Not accessible in the game as of 7.1; limited to the 1.6 and 2.8 event runs.
